summary: Weekly POC sync to review this week's benchmark results vs baseline provider. Redwood showed p50/p95 latency and throughput with batching + KV cache improvements; baseline (ProviderX) numbers used for comparison. Major themes: tail latency improvements with cache, cost/latency tradeoffs, dedicated pool request for a short trial. Action items agreed to share raw logs, run 8k context tests, and schedule dedicated pool trial.
transcript:
[00:00] Marcus Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Marcus from Redwood here, AE. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Samantha Ortiz: Sam from Arcadia, hi.
[00:08] Daniel Kim: Daniel, infra.
[00:10] Priya Patel: Priya, CTO.
[00:12] Alex Rivera: Alex, SRE.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Priya Nair, Redwood SE.
[00:18] Jordan Wu: Jordan, Redwood CSM.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: Cool, thanks. Agenda — quick recap, benchmark numbers vs ProviderX baseline, dig into p95 tail, then next steps.
[00:30] Samantha Ortiz: Sounds good. We got your note, excited to see the numbers.
[00:34] Priya Nair: Great. I'll share my screen, going to walk through the dashboard we ran yesterday, and then the raw timeseries we captured. Apologies if some labels are a bit off — the exporter renamed a couple things.
[00:46] Marcus Lee: No worries.
[00:48] Priya Nair: Ok first slide — p50 latency for our hosted Redwood config with continuous batching and prefix KV cache was ~72ms for a 2k average request size, that's 12% better than ProviderX which measured at 82ms under the same synthetic load. p95 is where it gets more interesting: Redwood p95 was 210ms vs ProviderX 360ms.
[01:12] Daniel Kim: Wait, is that with quantized model or full fp16?
[01:15] Priya Nair: This set was int8 quantized on A100s, baseline was ProviderX using their standard fp16 endpoint for the same model. We also ran an fp16 Redwood run — p95 bumped to ~290ms, so quantization bought about 25% improvement on tails.
[01:29] Alex Rivera: And what was the throughput? We care about sustained RPS.
[01:33] Priya Nair: Sustained throughput with batching set to target 64 tokens per batch was 320 requests/minute for 2k prompt sizes. ProviderX sustained ~240 r/min under same concurrency profile. We saw better packing on our continuous batching plus lower scheduler jitter.
[01:48] Samantha Ortiz: Those numbers look promising. How consistent are they? Any spikes during the run?
[01:53] Priya Nair: Good question. We logged over a 30-minute window — there were a few spikes on the ProviderX runs correlated with cold-start-like variance. On Redwood the spikes were mostly at the start of the run when KV cache warming happened. After warmup, tail percentiles stabilized.
[02:11] Marcus Lee: We should call out the workload shape — we used your real traces, right? Sam, you shared production-ish traces trimmed to 2k average length?
[02:20] Samantha Ortiz: Yes we shared last week's trace file, sampled to 1000 requests. We kept the same seq length distribution.
[02:25] Priya Nair: Right, we re-played the trace in the benchmarking harness. One note though: ProviderX's metric labeling slipped on token counts so their numbers may underreport token-level batching efficiency. We flagged that but still included them as baseline.
[02:40] Daniel Kim: On the caching — KV cache only helps for repeated prefixes, do we have a sense of reuse in our trace?
[02:46] Priya Nair: We measured ~18% prefix reuse across sessions which explains some of the tail improvement. Also we applied prefix caching at the session layer which reduced repeated attention recompute.
[02:58] Priya Patel: For compliance we need to know if logs include any PII and where they land.
[03:03] Jordan Wu: Jordan here — we redacted all user PII for these runs. Raw logs we're planning to share will exclude PII; we'll also provide guidance on storage locations and KMS options.
[03:13] Alex Rivera: KMS integration — do you support customer-managed keys in the private deployment?
[03:17] Marcus Lee: Yes, Private supports KMS/HSM integrations. For hosted we have envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS in Dedicated or Private. We'll send the security docs.
[03:26] Samantha Ortiz: Good. Back to latency: you mentioned batching 64 tokens — what was the latency tradeoff for cold single-request paths?
[03:33] Priya Nair: We use adaptive batching with latency SLOs configured. For single-request cold path p50 was ~95ms, p95 320ms; once KV warmed and batching kicked in it got down to the numbers I mentioned. There's always a small cold penalty but we can adjust autoscale and burst capacity for interactive SLAs.
[03:49] Daniel Kim: Baseline provider — do they offer a dedicated pool? Because our procurement will want to compare dedicated pricing.
[03:55] Marcus Lee: ProviderX has a dedicated offering but it's more expensive and less flexible. Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved capacity with configurable autoscale and burst, and we can do a short dedicated trial so you can validate sustained throughput under your workload.
[04:08] Priya Patel: Trial logistics — what does a trial look like? Timeboxed reserved capacity?
[04:13] Jordan Wu: Typically a 2-week reserved pool with monitoring access, cost estimate, and an ops runbook. We'll also include playbook for fallback policies.
[04:21] Samantha Ortiz: We'd like to test 8k context and LLama-like long context behavior too. Our product team wants to push context for certain features.
[04:28] Priya Nair: Noted — we'll run 8k-context tests and share latency/throughput as well. Quantization profile might differ for long contexts.
[04:34] Daniel Kim: About accuracy — quantizing to int8, any observed regressions? We need quality thresholds.
[04:39] Priya Nair: We ran a subset of your eval prompts — small drop in a few QA items, about 1.8% relative; most customers find int8 acceptable for production, but we can pin fp16 for high-sensitivity flows. Redwood Optimize can recommend per-route quantization.
[04:54] Marcus Lee: Ok, let's cover cost delta: rough numbers?
[04:57] Jordan Wu: For the pilot config used in the benchmark — int8 hosted calls, average token lengths, the per-1M-token unit cost was ~20% lower than ProviderX's hosted fp16 pricing in our quote. With Dedicated the unit cost drops further depending on commit. We'll send detailed pricing.
[05:13] Samantha Ortiz: Excellent. On security docs — please send SOC2 and KMS details. Priya Patel will review.
[05:18] Priya Patel: Yep.
[05:20] Marcus Lee: All right, quick recap of action items then next steps — Marcus to share spreadsheet, Priya to run 8k test and long context runs, Jordan to prepare trial estimate and timeline, Sam to confirm stakeholders. Any other blockers?
[05:34] Samantha Ortiz: Only procurement approval — we'll loop in procurement once we see the pricing.
[05:39] Daniel Kim: And SRE will want to run the trial traffic shaping, Alex will coordinate.
[05:43] Alex Rivera: Yep will do.
[05:45] Marcus Lee: Great. Any remaining questions?
[05:47] Samantha Ortiz: One small one — did you test model fallbacks if the dedicated pool is saturated?
[05:52] Priya Nair: We did a failover test — automatic routing to a smaller compatible variant with a slight latency increase but kept request success rate high. We can include the policy in the runbook.
[06:03] Marcus Lee: Perfect. We'll send the logs and spreadsheet by Friday, set up the dedicated trial next week pending procurement thumbs-up. Thanks all.
[06:12] Samantha Ortiz: Thanks everyone.
[06:14] --- (end of recorded transcript)

Notes: transcription contains minor label noise and occasional filler words. Some provider names may be anonymized as ProviderX for competitive neutrality. The benchmark artifacts referenced (spreadsheet + raw logs) will be attached to CRM record after export.
